title: The Monster in the Pacific
lines: Something is waking up in the Pacific. | And it could break the world's heat record.
It's called El Niño: | when the trade winds weaken, | a giant pool of warm water spreads east across the ocean.
Right now, parts of the Pacific are three degrees hotter than normal. | A warm stripe more than {10,000 km~ten thousand kilometres} long.
Most forecasts say it will become the strongest El Niño ever measured. | Even stronger than the "Godzilla" El Niño of {2015~twenty fifteen}.
It moves rain around the planet: | droughts in Australia and the Amazon, | floods in the Americas and East Africa. | Crops can fail, and food prices can climb.
And on top of global warming, | it could make {2027~twenty twenty-seven} the hottest year ever recorded. | One leading climate scientist puts the odds at {95%~ninety-five percent}.
Is your weather already strange? | Tell me in the comments.
